title: Bijendra Singh v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Siddhartha Varma and Manoj Bajaj, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed of; petitioner relegated to Ombudsman under clause 7.10(iv).
headnote: Writ challenging the District Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission's order dated 25.05.2023 was disposed of on the Electricity Department's plea that an appeal to the Ombudsman under clause 7.10(iv) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is an efficacious alternative remedy. If the petitioner approaches the Ombudsman under that clause within three weeks, the Ombudsman shall decide the matter in accordance with law within two months of filing.
facts: Bijendra Singh invoked the writ jurisdiction of the Allahabad High Court against the order dated 25 May 2023 of the District Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission, Gautam Buddha Nagar. The State of Uttar Pradesh and five others were respondents. Counsel for the Electricity Department submitted at the hearing that the petitioner had an efficacious alternative remedy of an appeal to the Ombudsman under clause 7.10(iv) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

holding_units.holding: The writ challenging the District Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission's order dated 25.05.2023 was disposed of on counsel's statement that an efficacious alternative remedy of appeal lies before the Ombudsman under clause 7.10(iv) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If the petitioner approaches the Ombudsman under that clause within three weeks, the Ombudsman shall dispose of the matter in accordance with law within two months of filing.

principle_tags.application: The Division Bench treated an appeal to the Ombudsman under clause 7.10(iv) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 as an efficacious alternative to the writ and disposed of the petition on that basis, allowing three weeks to approach the Ombudsman and two months for disposal.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the District Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission's order dated 25.05.2023
not_decided.note: The writ was disposed without examining that order. The grievance is for the Ombudsman if the petitioner files under clause 7.10(iv) within three weeks.
